newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Friday on a technical rebound supported by short-covering after sharp price falls on Thursday, traders said.
But market fundamentals remained poor despite the rises and there was little potential for further hikes early next week, they said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 23,430 ($2,825) yuan per tonne, up 60 yuan. It opened up at 23,400 and hit a low of 23,310 early in trading.
June rose 70 to 22,770, July 50 to 22,940, August 20 to 23,150, October 30 to 23,460 and November 40 to 23,450 tonnes.
Combined volume rose to 39,780 tonnes from 35,390 tonnes.
Traders said the day's rises were supported by short-covering and speculative buying after the losses.
"But the major September and October contracts were still below the 23,500-yuan resistance level at the close, indicating a downward trend has not been reversed," one trader said.
Traders said they believed the major contracts would continue to meet resistance at that level next Monday.
Physical prices moved back up to 23,100 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, up from 23,000 in the morning, traders said.
June fell 40 to 14,910, July fell 50 to 14,950, August did not trade, September lost 50 to 15,300, October rose 20 to 15,320 and November closed unchanged at 15,300 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 2,240 tonnes from 1,340 tonnes.
